capitals.name: Suktimati (Sotthivati; near Banda or Itaha/Rewa)
capitals.note: The location 'has not been established with certainty': Raychaudhuri and Pargiter placed it 'in the vicinity of Banda, Uttar Pradesh', Chakrabarti at the ruins of 'Itaha, on the outskirts of Rewa, Madhya Pradesh' (24.53N 81.30E). Coordinates are Banda's.

correction.text: Cedi in 'the eastern part of the modern-day Bundelkhand' near the Yamuna, around the two proposed sites of its capital Suktimati, 'in the vicinity of Banda, Uttar Pradesh' and 'Itaha, on the outskirts of Rewa, Madhya Pradesh'

keyframe_review.note: The 4,396 km2 shape (centroid 81.43E 25.53N) sits on the Yamuna at Kausambi, inside Vatsa's land (Cliopatria lists janapada-of-vatsa as a neighbour within 25 km); the page puts Cedi in eastern Bundelkhand with its capital near Banda (80.34E 25.48N, 110 km west) or Itaha near Rewa, and the Mahajanapadas page has the Chedis 'midway between the kingdom of Kurus and Vatsas'. The corrected shape (about 35,000 km2) covers both candidate capitals. The infobox gives no area. Banda (India) and Rewa are not in the gazetteer.

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Cedi, one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, is ruled from Suktimati in eastern Bundelkhand. 'By the 6th to 5th centuries BCE' Cedi was 'one of the more important states in Iron Age India' and the Anguttara Nikaya listed it among the 'solasa Mahajanapadas'; infobox 'Established c. 1200 BCE', 'Capital Suktimati or Sotthivati'. -600 is the Mahajanapada convention; the Vedic Cedi of king Caidya (Rgveda) is left to batch sa-01-x.

ledger.note: c. 450 BCE: Cedi disappears from the record (Cliopatria's end). The page gives 'Disestablished c. 300 BCE' and nothing on how the state ended; the Mahajanapadas page is silent too. Cliopatria ends the row in -451, the year it also ends Vatsa; no page names a conqueror, so no successor is recorded and the land is drawn as nobody's until the Shaishunaga shape (-404) covers it. A gap-filler with the Nanda and Shaishunaga pages should settle whether Cedi lasted to c. 300 BCE as a dependency.

certainty.note: The page gives neighbours (Matsya beyond the Chambal to the west, Kasi to the north-east, the Karusas in the Son valley to the east, the Dasarnas on the Dhasan) but no line; the shape is two radii around the candidate capitals.

sources.title: Mahajanapadas
sources.note: Overview of the sixteen states ('from the sixth to fourth centuries BCE'), the Mahajanapada convention behind every -600 start, and the per-state location notes; shared by the five janapada dossiers of batch sa-01-a.

notes: Cliopatria's two identical shapes sit at Kausambi, in Vatsa's land, 110 km east of where the page puts Cedi; both are moved to eastern Bundelkhand (adjust). Nothing dated exists between the Mahajanapada convention (-600) and the infobox's 'c. 300 BCE' end; Cliopatria's -451 end is kept at confidence 1 with no successor, because neither page names a conqueror (a gap, not a fact). The later Chedi of Kalinga and the Kalachuris are unrelated to this row. Gazetteer names lacking: places Banda (Uttar Pradesh, 25.48N 80.34E) and Rewa (Madhya Pradesh, 24.53N 81.30E); the gazetteer's 'Banda' hits are Indonesian.
